records.name: The Youth Sexpert Program
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches high school age youth about sexual health, so they can learn accurate facts about sex, consent and staying healthy. The fall cohort meets online and covers body knowledge, birth control and reducing stigma around STIs.
records.what_you_do: Participants meet online for lessons on sexual health, consent and communication skills. Taking part does not require teaching classes or workshops for other students.

schedule.text: Fall cohorts meet online. The site does not list days, times or cohort dates.

cost.text: The fall cohort page does not state a fee, stipend or price.

first_step.how: Fill in the Apply for Fall 2026 form linked from theyouthsexpertprogram.org.
first_step.basis: Joining needs an application, and the site gives no cohort dates, cost or sample session, so a newcomer cannot see what it is like first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The fall cohort is taught online, so a first visit means logging in from home. The site does not say how long the cohort runs, how many sessions there are, or what a session looks like. Topics include anatomy, birth control, consent, and queerness.
first_visit_tips: Email tara@theyouthsexpertprogram.org with questions about dates and cost before you apply.
Have a device and a steady internet connection for online sessions.

records.notes: The /program page returned 404, so program details come from the homepage and the Fall cohorts page. The cohort page lists high school age youth; the tier 1 record also listed young adults, which is kept because the audience for the separate weekend intensives is not stated. Cohort dates, cost and session count are not published. The homepage mentions Fall 2026 without a month, so last_sign_of_life is left out and status stays probably_active. Participants are not required to host peer classes, so the tier 1 wording about sharing with friends was softened. A separate donation page (givebutter) describes in-person weekend sex ed for teens in Texas and Georgia; that is not a Philadelphia option and is not in this record. Duplicate IRS address row removed.

records.name: Zia: Food You Can Count On
records.summary: A charity that brings healthy food to Philadelphia schoolchildren and their families. It runs a pantry for about forty member families, and volunteers pick up produce, pack meals and deliver them each week.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can pick up produce on Friday mornings, or pack meals and drive deliveries on Saturday mornings. Families can ask about joining the pantry, and anyone can give through the donate page.

schedule.text: Morning volunteer shifts: produce pickup on Fridays, and pantry packing and deliveries on Saturdays.

cost.text: No fee for families or volunteers is listed on the pages read. Online donations are accepted.

requirements.gear: Your own vehicle for the Friday pickup and the Saturday delivery shifts.

first_step.how: Fill in the form on the Volunteer With Us page at ziafood.org with your name, phone and email, then pick a Friday or Saturday shift.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page has a clear form and posted shift times, and it allows as little as one shift a month, but it does not say whether new volunteers get training.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers pick up produce, pack meals, or drive deliveries in short morning shifts. The volunteer page says the work is run out of First Presbyterian Church in Philadelphia, and it gives no street address.
first_visit_tips: Pickup and delivery volunteers need their own vehicle.
Shift times are 9 to 11:30 am Friday for produce, 9 to 11 am Saturday for packing, and 10 am to noon Saturday for deliveries.
Ask for the street address before your first shift, since the site gives none.

records.notes: The volunteer page places the volunteer work at First Presbyterian Church in Philadelphia, but the homepage describes the pantry at a partner elementary school. Neither page gives a street address, so no location was added beyond the IRS mailing addresses. The program page does not say how families join or who is eligible, and no page read states it. Days and times come from the volunteer page; tier 1 had none. Social links are from the homepage.

records.name: Chinese American Chamber of Commerce
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps Chinese Americans with business. It offers business education, networking events and grant-writing help, and it runs an awards program.
records.what_you_do: Watch the events page for networking events and business workshops, though no dated sessions were listed when checked. You can also apply to become a member.

cost.text: Membership fees are not shown on the pages read, and event prices were not listed when checked.

first_step.how: Use the join link on caccc.us to start a membership application, or email info@caccc.us to ask whether non-members can attend a networking event.
first_step.basis: Membership has a clear application page, but the site does not say whether workshops and networking events are open to non-members, and no dated events were listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes business workshops, networking events, and cultural programs, but when checked it listed no dates, places, or prices.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether non-members can come before you pay for anything.
Ask for the street address of the event, since the site gives only the city.

records.notes: Membership levels, benefits and eligibility are not stated on the pages read: the levels page has no tier names or dues, the benefits page has no text, and the application page shows only an email box. The events page lists a grand opening dated 1/29/2025 and an America250 event with no date, so no event in the last 12 months is dated. The site gives only Philadelphia as the office location. A footer also lists CACCC.US@gmail.com, which is not recorded. Tier 1 listed the same IRS address twice; one row kept.

records.name: Loverock Nonprofit Charitable Foundation
records.summary: A small charity that helps people in Philadelphia who are homeless or short of money. Volunteers take meals and hygiene gift bags out to people on the street and to shelters, and the group also helps with clothing and medical needs.
records.what_you_do: Helpers pack meals and care packages into cars and drive them out to people on the streets and in shelters. Call the group to ask how to join the outreach, or how to get help yourself.

schedule.text: Food and care-package outings happen twice a month, on Tuesdays and Fridays.

cost.text: The site does not state a cost for any service, and it asks for donations.

first_step.how: Call 215-730-5677 and ask how to join the street outreach.
first_step.basis: The site lists a phone number and a contact form, but it describes no sign-up steps, training, or meeting place for volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers load meals and care packages into cars and head out to share them twice a month. The site does not say how long an outing lasts, where to meet, or whether you need training first.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come, since the site gives no meeting place.
Ask whether you can help on a single outing before you commit to more.

records.notes: The About page says outings run twice a month on Tuesdays and Fridays, while the food program page says days are not stated; the record uses the About page. There is no volunteer page, no sign-up steps, and no office address; the site lists only Philadelphia, PA. The sister group, Theresa Nonprofit Foundation (diabetes), is named on the site and is in leads_only. Tier 1 listed the same IRS address twice; one row kept.

records.name: 3rd Awakening USA
records.summary: A Christian revival movement that holds worship gatherings and outreach in streets, schools and churches. Members can join outreach teams, take part in prayer efforts, or host an event in their own city.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to serve on a team for event setup, street outreach, prayer, or media work, join the prayer team, or apply to host an event in your city.

cost.text: The site mentions no fee to join or volunteer. Giving is optional.

first_step.how: Open the Get Involved page on 3rdawakeningusa.org, use the Sign Up to Serve button, and pick a role such as event setup or prayer.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to sign up, but names no city, meeting place, training, or schedule, so the local way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists volunteer roles in event setup and logistics, street evangelism, prayer ministry, and media or content work. It does not give a schedule, a meeting place, or how long a shift runs.
first_visit_tips: Ask what the street evangelism role involves before you agree to it.
Ask which city has an active outreach team, since the site names no local group.
The events page showed no upcoming events when checked, so ask about the next one.

records.notes: Checked the What We Do page for partisan political content: none found. The seven pillars page was not read. Kind changed from congregation to network because the group works through partner churches and does not describe a congregation of its own. The site names no cities, meeting places or schedule. The events page shows no upcoming events and one past event with no visible date. The email comes from the Contact Us link (mailto), and its domain is .com while the website is .org.

records.name: Camp Jamison
records.summary: A one-week overnight summer camp for kids 8 to 15 from the Philadelphia area. Campers hike, swim, paddle on the lake, play sports, make art, and sit around the campfire.
records.what_you_do: Campers spend a week at camp each summer. The camp also hires cabin counselors and activity specialists, and donors can help fund campers through a memorial scholarship.

schedule.text: One week of overnight camp each summer, 7 days and 6 nights.

cost.text: The base fee is $200 for each camper. Higher payment levels, from $201 up, help cover supplies, transportation, staff and year-round costs.

requirements.gear: A packing list is on the campers page. It includes a sleeping bag, sheets, towels, sturdy sneakers, and a reusable water bottle.

first_step.how: Fill in the online registration form for the summer session, linked from campjamison.org, or join the waiting list for updates.
first_step.basis: Registration for kids 8 to 15 runs through a public form with a clear link, although the site also offers a waiting list, so spots may be limited.
first_step.what_to_expect: Campers stay seven days and six nights at a camp with a lake, campground areas, and hiking trails. The site lists canoeing, kayaking, lake swimming, hiking, basketball, GaGa ball, arts and crafts, and campfires with s'mores.
first_visit_tips: Bring the listed items: a sleeping bag, a twin fitted sheet, two pairs of sturdy sneakers (one that can get wet), and a reusable water bottle.
Leave electronics, toys, snacks, and scented items at home, since the list bans them.
Label all belongings, because the camp is not responsible for lost items.
Ask for drop-off and pick-up times when you register, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: The site gives two staff email addresses that disagree: the text names jacqueline@campjamison.org, while the staff application link goes to jchristy@campjamison.org. The record uses the jacqueline address. The 2026 session dates (July 19 to 25, extended to July 29) are one-time dates, so they are not in schedule text, and last_sign_of_life is unchanged. No street address, drop-off times, daily schedule, staff age minimum or staff pay are stated. The cell phone policy page was not read.

records.name: East Torresdale Civic Association
records.summary: A City-registered neighborhood group in the Lower Far Northeast. The City lists it to hear about zoning and development proposals in its area.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over.

locations.label: Address on City list
locations.address: All Saints Episcopal Church, 9601 Frankford Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19114

first_step.how: Email Joseph Carson at the address on the City's list to ask when and where the next meeting is.

records.notes: The group's own site (easttorresdalecivic.com) and its membership portal (etca-rco.clubexpress.com) both returned HTTP 403, so no deeper detail was gathered and this record holds tier 1 facts only. A web search turned up a meeting schedule and attendance rules, but I could not open a page that states them, so they are not recorded; they are worth checking on a later pass. The website host is written in lower case.
